archetype.name: Rebuilding Year (offense ahead of pitching)
archetype.definition: A 104-loss season that was still a 15-win recovery from 2025's floor, driven by a lineup that climbed from 29th to 7th in scoring while the pitching staff finished last in run prevention for a fifth straight year.

report.headline: Fifteen wins better than 2025, but pitching kept Colorado buried at the bottom

recap.finish: 58-104, fifth in the NL West, 42 games behind LAD; missed the postseason
recap.body:
The 2026 Rockies were a bad team that was much less bad than the year before. Going from 43-119 to 58-104 is a real climb, and the run differential nearly halved, from -2.62 per game to -1.19. They still finished seven games behind fourth-place San Francisco and 27th on the site's Teams tab. The progress was real, but it came from a very low base.

The season had a short honeymoon. After a 1-4 opening week, they went 13-14 in April and scored and allowed runs at nearly the same rate. Then May hit: 8-20, with 190 runs allowed in 28 games, close to seven a night. June (11-15) and July (10-14, outscored by only 8) were respectable by this franchise's recent standards. The finish was ugly, though. They went 9-19 in August and 6-18 in September, closing 2-8 over the last ten games and 15-37 over the final two months. A four-game win streak was the longest of the year.

The lineup was the reason for the improvement, but the park inflates how good it looks. A 7th-place offense rank and the 5th-best OPS (.739) come with a 125 park factor. The park-adjusted wRC+ figures tell a narrower story. TJ Rumfield (124, .390 OBP) was the best bat, and Hunter Goodman's 41 homers earned him an All-Star nod at catcher. Jake McCarthy (108, 32 steals) led the team in WAR, and Kyle Karros added a solid 2.0 WAR at third. Past those four, the regulars sat at or below average. Ezequiel Tovar's 55 wRC+ over 506 plate appearances was the biggest hole in the lineup. The C- hitter grade fits: a few real pieces surrounded by filler.

Run prevention sank everything else. A 5.59 ERA ranked dead last, the rotation graded F and the bullpen D-. This is the fifth year running at 30th in runs allowed. Some of that ERA was not the pitchers' doing. Kyle Freeland (6.65 ERA, 5.09 FIP), Tanner Gordon (6.68 vs 4.85) and Gabriel Hughes (6.33 vs 4.04) all allowed far more runs than their strikeouts, walks and homers would predict. That fits a defense at -25.6 Fielding Runs, 27th in the league, a sharp drop from +28.4 in 2023. Even so, FIPs near 5 are not good. Tomoyuki Sugano's 14.6% strikeout rate is the clearest sign of a staff that can't miss bats, and in this park that is fatal. Brennan Bernardino (2.81 ERA in 74 games) was the lone reliable arm.

Luck didn't help either. The W vs Run Diff mark of -6.4 says this run differential normally produces about 64 wins. That would still be a miserable season, but it means the 58-104 record understates the improvement somewhat.

highlights.title: Lineup climbed from 29th to 7th
highlights.body: Runs per game jumped from 29th in 2025 to 7th, and team OPS rose from .679 to .739 in the same park. Rumfield, Goodman and McCarthy all posted above-average wRC+ figures, and those three plus Karros produced most of the hitters' WAR. The core is young enough on these numbers to carry forward, though the park makes the raw totals look better than they are.

highlights.title: Fifteen-win jump, run differential halved
highlights.body: The record moved from 43-119 to 58-104, and the run differential improved by more than a run per game. Unlike some improvements, this one wasn't flattered by luck. The team actually underperformed its differential by about six wins, so the underlying gain is larger than the record shows.

lowlights.title: Last in run prevention again
lowlights.body: A 5.59 ERA and an F rotation grade made this the fifth straight year at 30th in runs allowed, so this is not one bad season. The starters' low strikeout rates mean too many balls in play in an extreme hitters' park. Several ERAs sat well above their FIPs, which points partly to bad luck and partly to the defense behind them.

lowlights.title: Defense turned into a liability
lowlights.body: Fielding Runs of -25.6 ranked 27th, a big swing from the positive marks of 2021 through 2024. Willi Castro and McCarthy were among the regulars below average in the field. The gap between ERA and FIP for several starters suggests the defense added real runs to an already overmatched staff.

lowlights.title: Tovar's bat bottomed out
lowlights.body: Ezequiel Tovar played 146 games with a 55 wRC+ and .264 OBP, finishing at -0.4 WAR, the worst of any regular. With his glove also grading below average, shortstop was the lineup's biggest drain.

arc.note: A near-.500 April gave way to an 8-20 May. June and July were competitive, and then the team collapsed to 15-37 over August and September.

recap.nextYear: Rumfield, Goodman, McCarthy and Karros form a lineup core worth building around. The rest of the order, Tovar above all, needs upgrades to push the C- hitter grade higher. Some regression is likely to help: a -6.4 W vs Run Diff tends to even out, and several starters' ERAs ran well above their FIPs, so the run total allowed should come down if the defense recovers toward its earlier positive marks. That only gets the staff from awful to bad. The rotation's strikeout rates, mostly 15-18%, are a structural problem, and only Hughes (4.04 FIP in 64 innings) and the injured Chase Dollander (24.9% strikeout rate) showed swing-and-miss worth projecting. Bernardino is the only bullpen arm the numbers trust. Until the pitching gets out of 30th, the improved offense can only shrink the losses.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season with five years of history confirming the pitching pattern.
